newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index falls in easy trade week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index falls in easy trade week.

text.p: Kuwait Stock Exchange's index fell 20.2 points to 2,364.5 in an easy trade week with investors anticipating mid-year results of listed firms, dealers said on Thursday.
"The market is usually quite ahead of mid-year results," said a private dealer. "Also, many investors are abroad" for summer vacations, he added.
All listed firms are required by law to issue their mid-year results in the weeks following July 1.
Dealers also said the market is still depressed by Central Bank curbs on lending for equity trading introduced less than a month ago.
"The rules reduced liquidity in the market," said an economist.

The Central Bank, in a risk controlling move, asked domestic banks in May to cut outstanding loans extended for equity trading to about 295 million dinars ($977 million) from 425 million by the end of 1997.
The move followed overheated activity that triggered correction warnings by some economists.
Losers led gainers 28-15 while 25 shares did not move.

Daily average for value of traded shares fell to 27.8 million dinars from 45.5 million. Volume eased to a daily average of 93.7 million shares from 155.8 million, Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) figures show.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 35.5 million dinars, followed by property firms with 34.2 million and industrials with 38.4 million.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
